account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment book: morning correspondence, a ten o'clock market walk, lunch at home, and town accounts at one. The treasury contains 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. During the market walk, townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery; that sounds like ordinary bread-making business, not evidence of anything unusual.

The unusual matter is the three o'clock tea appointment. The book says only 'neighbour, dockside cottage, east bank,' without naming the host or giving a precise cottage. The secretary has the appointment book and went to ask around the dockside cottages and warehouse. She returned before tea but could not identify the host, and several cottages had nobody answering. I have no invitation or other correspondence with me to clarify it. This may simply be an incomplete appointment entry; I have no evidence of any other purpose or scheme.

It is now 14:07, and I am at the town hall with the secretary. I have told her I will visit the dockside cottages and ask directly, while she keeps new messages here. I intend to keep the tea appointment if I can identify the host, then return to the office at 16:30 and go home at 19:00.
